text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- Romania's new Foreign Minister Adrian Severin arrived in Budapest Thursday for talks with his Hungarian counterpart Laszlo Kovacs and to exchange the ratification documents of the Romanian-Hungarian basic treaty signed earlier this year. Severin said he sees no obstactles to Hungary opening a consulate general in Cluj-Napoca. @

- The price of various services will go up January 1, led by a 31 percent increase in the price of local telephone calls. Water and sewerage bills are set to go up by 24.2 percent on average. Train fares will rise by 18 percent, goods transport by 20 percent, inter-city bus tickets will be 19.8 percent more expensive. Budapest transit tickets will cost 24.9 percent more. Domestic postal services will be 17.9 percent higher.

- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. saw a deficit of HUF 4.5 billion through the end of November despite HUF 109.92 billion in cash and almost HUF 35 billion in other revenues from the privatisation of 175 companies. @
- Temperatures over the next few days are forecast to be the lowest this century in Hungary, dropping to -25 Celsius in the northeastern part of the country.
- At least five people died of exposure during the extremely cold weather at Christmas.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Parliament sat for 784 hours in plenary sessions over 98 days this year, passing 75 new acts, amending 57 others and debating 120 parliamentary resolutions. @

- Hungary's birth rate in 1996 will be its lowest this century, according to the Central Statistics Office, at 107,000. The overall population is estimated at 10,174,000 by the end of the year, 400,000 below the 1976 figure.

- Ethnic Hungarian Pal Cseresznyes was freed from prison in Romania after being pardoned by President Emil Constantinescu. Cseresznyes was imprisoned for assaulting a Romanian man in Tirgu Mures during an outbreak of ethnic strife in Transylvania in the March 1990 events.
MAGYAR NEMZET @
- Constitutional judge Peter Schmidt, who is turning 70, is retiring as of today, leaving the Constitutional Court members at nine, with two seats vacant.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The Tax Authority expects to meet its targets this year and see a total of HUF 1,306-1,318 billion in five major tax categories, and plans to boost this total by more than HUF 240 billion, or nearly 19 percent, in 1997. @

- State Banking Supervision (SBS) chief Imre Tarafas is the sole candidate to head a new institution to be established January 1 with the merger of the SBS and the State Securities and Exchange Commission.
- This economic daily has awarded its "Scoop of the Year" prize and the HUF 200,000 that went along with it to reporter Ildiko Nagy, who uncovered the Tocsik scandal earlier this year.
NAPI GAZDASAG @
- While the total volume of 1996 trade between Hungary and Croatia is expected to reach HUF 150 million by year's end, this sum could well grow ten-fold within the next two years.

- Merrill Lynch and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell are still in the running to manage the projected $500 million issue, which would represent 16 percent of Matav's capital and be among the region's largest share issues ever.
